前言

en: The initial scope of these pages is to test the waters of the relation between the theory of memory and the philosophy of history. The functioning of the mnestic faculty, its performances and pathologies, may perhaps be able to provide us with categories and a lexicon able to give account of historical experience, now that the ‘bordello of historicism’ (as Walter Benjamin put it, not too tactfully
) has pulled up the shutters.
zh: 这几页文字首先试图探讨记忆理论与历史哲学之间的关系。记忆官能（mnestic faculty）的运作、表现及其病理，或许能为我们提供一套范畴和词汇，用以说明历史经验——尤其是在“历史主义的妓院（im Bordell des Historismus）”（用瓦尔特·本雅明那句并不委婉的话说）
已然开门迎客的今日。

en: This theme lends itself to a number of ambiguities. We should shake off at least some of these immediately. First off, we are certainly not going to set about comparing the collective past to Proust’s Combray, or reducing the challenge of historiography to nibbling on

. To miniaturise history, hemming it into the cassock of ‘lived experience’, is a miserable fallback solution, one that should be given a wide berth. Such a response is simply the prophylactic measure (or expedient consolation prize) of those who, whatever their recalcitrance, have proven unable to free themselves from the spell of the historicist ‘bordello’. Here, instead, we want to trace out a totally different path. Rather than constipate the

and the narration of them within the limits of biographical commemoration, we need to grasp the non-psychological, supra-personal, public significance of the concepts with which we analyse the formation – as well as the deterioration – of memory.
zh: 这个主题容易引起若干歧义，其中一些应立即加以澄清。首先，我们当然不是要把集体的过去比作普鲁斯特笔下的贡布雷，也不是要把史学的难题化约为品尝小玛德莱娜蛋糕。
把历史微缩化，硬塞进“亲历经验（lived experience）”的僧袍，是应当回避的糟糕退路。这样的回应，不过是那些始终无法摆脱历史主义“妓院”魅惑的人——无论他们如何抗拒——所采取的防护措施
，或是权宜的安慰奖。我们要开辟一条全然不同的道路：与其把历史事实（res gestae）及其叙述局限于个人生平的追忆，不如把握我们借以分析记忆之形成及其衰退的那些概念所具有的非心理学、超个人和公共意义。

en: But what do we mean, when we speak of the supra-personal meaning of mnestic processes? Here a second ambiguity comes into view, opposed to and mirroring the first. It is called ‘historical memory’. As we know, this formula is used to designate awareness of events that have taken place and of their lasting influence on actuality. But we are grappling with a misleading metaphor here: we ought instead to speak of historical culture or consciousness, rather than of memory. And yet, mind, it is precisely in order to determine the forms – but also the crisis – of such consciousness or culture (and, therefore, of this ‘historical memory’ itself) that it is perhaps necessary for us to turn back to the conceptual constellation pertaining … to memory, in the strict sense (the memory with which each person is endowed from infancy). As such, from the outset this ambiguous little formula takes for granted precisely the problem that it poses, one that is still to be answered. Memory is not ‘historical’ in virtue of the particular content (for example, the social or political content) of memories. Rather, it is historical in that it is that

that distinguishes individual existence. Indeed, the structure and processes of this faculty provide an access route to the historicity of experience – of any experience, of experience in general. Memory, which is always memory of the particular, however, constitutes a sort of ‘ontogenetic recapitulation’ of the various modes of being historical, as well as the formal matrix of historiographical categories. Precisely and only
in this sense does it have a supra-personal value and a public character.
zh: 然而，所谓记忆过程的超个人意义，究竟指什么？这时，另一重歧义进入视野；它与第一重歧义相反，却又同它互为镜像。这一歧义名叫“历史记忆”。众所周知，这个说法用来指称：人们意识到已经发生的事件，以及这些事件对现实持续产生的影响。但我们面对的其实是一个误导性的隐喻：严格说来，与其称之为记忆，不如称之为历史文化或历史意识。尽管如此，请注意：恰恰为了确定这种意识或文化的形式——以及它的危机——从而也为了确定这种“历史记忆”本身，我们或许有必要重新考察围绕严格意义上的记忆——即每个人从婴儿时期便具有的记忆——形成的概念群。因此，这个含混的小小表述从一开始就把它所提出、却尚待解答的问题视为已有定论。记忆之所以是“历史的”，并不是因为记忆内容本身具有某种特殊性质（例如社会或政治内容）；记忆之所以是历史的，是因为记忆正是个体存在所特有的官能。事实上，这一官能的结构和过程，为我们通向经验的历史性（historicity）——任何经验乃至一般经验的历史性——提供了一条路径。记忆固然总是对个别事物的记忆，但它也构成了各种历史性存在方式的一种“个体发生式的重演（ontogenetic recapitulation）”，同时还是史学范畴的形式矩阵。正是在、也仅仅是在这个意义上，记忆才具有超个人的价值和公共性质。

en: I will give a few examples which are useful in terms of how we look at this problem. Psychiatrists and neurobiologists
count among the causes of memory-loss two types of
: the first, which they call
, is the disturbance that a new piece of information
introduces into the memory of a prior event; the second,
interference is, instead, the obstacle inherent in the currently

lived situation to memorising what will follow it. It is obvious enough what significance the study of the different types of ‘interference’ could have for the philosophy of history. Similarly, looking at the arena of historiography, it is not difficult to work out the relevance of the distinction between
(the past congealed in
or habit, conserved as a technique or ethos) and
(the explicit re-evocation of signs and meanings that are inherent to long-ago experiences). And, moreover, consider how prehensile and perspicacious notions such as the following could prove:
(increasing mnestic capacity in the event of crisis or trauma);
(to substitute a suddenly reflowering memory for a completely new idea); or

(to attribute to a past experience a content or context different to its real ones). Ultimately, might it not be the case that the old question raised by Augustine, of what the ‘memory of a memory’ is – and, above all, what the ‘memory of having forgotten’ is
– concerns the very core of all historical thought?
zh: 下面举几个有助于我们理解这个问题的例子。精神病学家和神经生物学家
把两类干扰列为记忆丧失的原因：第一类称为倒摄干扰，即一条新信息扰乱了对先前事件的记忆；第二类则称为前摄干扰，即当前

亲历的情境本身妨碍了我们记住随后将发生的事情。研究不同类型的“干扰”对于历史哲学可能具有何种意义，是相当明显的。同样，转向史学领域，我们也不难看出区分程序性记忆（凝结在实际技能或习惯中的过去，它以技术或习性的形式保存下来）与语义记忆（明确重新唤起久远经验中所含的符号和意义）的重要性。此外，还可以想想下列概念能多么敏锐地把握问题：记忆亢进（hypermnesia，在危机或创伤发生时记忆能力增强）；隐匿记忆（cryptomnesia，把一段突然重新浮现的记忆误当作全新的想法）；错构记忆（allomnesia，把不同于真实内容或语境的内容或语境归给某段过去经验）。最后，奥古斯丁提出的那个古老问题——什么是“对一段记忆的记忆”，尤其是什么是“对自己已经遗忘这件事的记忆”——难道不正触及一切历史思想的核心吗？

en: We shall dedicate the following pages, however, to one mnestic phenomenon only: namely, what we call the déjà vu. We do this out of the conviction that this specific pathology of memory can cast new light on a canonical theme of historical-philosophical reflection, which is also a pervasive, overbearing state of mind characteristic of the contemporary forms of life. This philosophical theme
– now also a recklessly advancing mood – is the theme of history stopping, or, more radically, the
zh: 不过，以下各页只讨论一种记忆现象，也就是我们所说的既视感（déjà vu）。我们之所以如此，是因为相信：这种特定的记忆病理能够为历史哲学反思中的一个经典主题投下新的光亮；与此同时，这个主题也是当代生活形式中一种无处不在、咄咄逼人的心境。这个哲学主题——如今也已经成为一种恣意蔓延的情绪——就是历史的停顿，或者更彻底地说，历史的终结。

瓦尔特·本雅明：《论历史的概念》，命题十六，见 marxists.org：“历史唯物主义者不能没有这样一种现在概念：这个现在不是过渡，而是时间在其中发源并停顿之处。因为这一概念恰恰规定了他为自己书写历史时所处的现在。历史主义描绘过去的‘永恒’图景；历史唯物主义者则提供一种独立无匹的过去经验。他任由别人投身于历史主义妓院里那个名叫‘从前’的娼妇。对于自己的力量，他始终作主：他有足够的男子气概，炸开历史的连续统。”
en: Walter Benjamin, ‘On the Concept of History’, Thesis XVI, at
: ‘The historical materialist cannot do without the concept of a present which is not a transition, in which time originates and has come to a standstill. For this concept defines precisely

present in which he writes history for his person. Historicism depicts the “eternal” picture of the past; the historical materialist, an experience with it, which stands alone. He leaves it to others to give themselves to the whore called “Once upon a time” in the bordello of historicism. He remains master of his powers: man enough, to explode the continuum of history.’

zh: 贡布雷（Combray）指普鲁斯特小说《追忆似水年华》中主人公童年时期的家乡贡布雷，小说中叙述者被玛德莱娜蛋糕（madeleines）意外唤起关于贡布雷童年的记忆，构成普鲁斯特的“非意愿记忆”意象。-中译者注

众所周知，卢梭借助一种生存官能——意志——阐发了其政治哲学的根本概念，尽管意志向来被视为一切官能中最内在、最个人也最隐秘的一种。卢梭谈到“公意”（volonté générale，亦即一般意志）。不那么广为人知、却同样重要（而且可以说敏锐得多）的，是马克思借助智力官能来指明社会最大的潜能，即各个生产者已经共同拥有的东西。马克思称之为“一般智力”（general intellect）。我们看待记忆官能时也不应有太大不同。正如正文所说，我们的目的是找到足以思考历史经验、更彻底地说足以思考经验之历史性的范畴。意志—政治、智力—社会关系、记忆—历史性？第一项联系会引起疑问——而且疑问不小——后两项却不会。通过研究生存官能，理解其中更为超个人（或较少“私人”）的部分，这项工作在奥古斯丁《论三位一体》第十卷中已有极其重要的先例。他在那里确立了圣父与记忆、圣子与智力、圣灵与意志之间的类比（更确切地说，是同构）。奥古斯丁并不把不完美模仿圣父特征的记忆看成一种可以与其他官能并列的普通官能；记忆反而同心灵的全部生命重合，是所有具体官能——首先是意志和智力——铭写于其中的范围或语境。记忆超越其他人类禀赋，恰如“存在”超越并包含其他每个范畴。此外，奥古斯丁在《忏悔录》第十三卷中把三位一体比作理性造物的三种特有能力：存在（取代记忆）、认识和意愿。关于这一点，见下文第二部分第八节。

none too differently. As we say in the main text, we do so with the objective of finding adequate categories for thinking historical experience, and more radically, the

. Will-Politics, Intellect-social relations, Memory-historicity? The first connection sparks doubt – a substantial one – but not the other two. The study of existential faculties in order to understand what about them is more supra-personal (or less ‘private’) has an all-important precedent in book X of Augustine’s

. There, he established an analogy (or better, an isomorphism) between the Father and memory, the Son and the intellect, and the Holy Spirit and will. Augustine does not consider memory, which imperfectly imitates the characteristics of the Father, to be just any kind of faculty, comparable to the others: rather, it coincides with the entire life of the mind; it is the ambit, or context, in which all the particular faculties are inscribed, starting with will and the intellect. Memory goes beyond the other human aptitudes in the very same way that ‘being’ goes beyond (and itself comprises) every other category. Moreover, in the thirteenth book of his
, Augustine compared the Trinity to three prerogatives of the rational creature:
(instead of memory), knowing and willing. On this point, see below, Part II,
section 8
